title: Customer usage deep-dive + engineering blockers (Jul 2026)
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Short synthesis from a 2-hour cross-functional session (CS + Product + Eng infra) where we mapped recurring customer behaviors to concrete feature asks and surfaced engineering impediments blocking low-risk fixes.
- Focus: customers using Redwood to run high-throughput text generation (chat + prompts) in hosted and private modes. Representative sample: 12 customers (mid-market to enterprise), logs + support threads + interview notes.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Three emergent customer painlines: 1) tail-latency spikes under medium burst traffic, 2) unpredictable cost oscillations (mix of batching misconfig + tokenization double-counts), 3) migration friction for private deployments (networking/KMS and model-version pinning).
- Quick wins that unblock many customers: smaller default batch-window for routes with latency SLOs, a tokenization reconciliation checklist + script, and a config template for Private customers that includes common VPC firewall rules and KMS patterns.
- Engineering blockers (detailed later) mostly fall into: missing observability for per-route batching behavior, inconsistent token counting between SDK and backend, and incomplete infra templates for on-prem network topologies.

Representative customer vignettes (anonymized):
1) "RetailBot" (enterprise, Dedicated) — intermittent 800–1200ms tail spikes when traffic shifts from 60 RPS -> 200 RPS; they saw 30% drop in successful requests during spikes. Reproducible with load harness. Root ask: automatic fallback to smaller batch windows or single-request path for latency-sensitive routes.
2) "DocsAssist" (SaaS startup, Hosted) — surprised by monthly bill increases after enabling streaming responses; suspicion that token counting doubled on streamed vs non-streamed responses. Ask: transparent token accounting table and billing trace per-request.
3) "FinAnalytics" (regulated, Private VPC) — blocked on deployment due to KMS key policy mismatch and a missing example CloudFormation/Terraform snippet for cross-account access. Ask: hardened Private deployment example + checklist.

Synthesis of recurring themes:
- Observability & debugging: Customers want per-request token/batching traces they can hand to their SREs. Current console gives per-route aggregates but not a lightweight per-request trace link.
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs: Many customers implicitly use the same route for both interactive and batch workloads, causing suboptimal batching (bad for latency). They ask for route-level presets or heuristics.
- Private onboarding friction: networking examples and KMS policy templates are the lowest-effort deliverables with high impact. On-prem documentation gaps are the blocker.
- SDK/Platform drift: The SDK sometimes counts tokens differently than the billing pipeline (edge cases with custom tokenizers, function-calls payloads).

Prioritized feature requests (ranked by immediate CS impact + implementation effort estimate):
1) Per-request trace link in Console (low-medium effort). Rationale: shortens TTR for billing/latency investigations. Impact: recurring support cases reduced by ~45% (estimate).
2) "Latency-first" route preset: route config that prioritizes latency (smaller batch window, prefer single-request path, disable speculative aggregation) (medium effort). Impact: high for chat/interactive customers.
3) Tokenization reconciliation tool + SDK check: small CLI script that compares SDK token counts vs backend for a sample payload set (low effort). Impact: addresses billing confusion.
4) Private onboarding template repo: VPC/KMS/Firewall - one terraform + one cloudformation example + troubleshooting checklist (low effort).
5) Dynamic fallback policy (auto-switch batch size based on recent p95/p99) (higher effort). Impact: long-term fix for tail spikes but requires infra changes and careful SLO definitions.

Quick fixes / experiments to run in next sprint (owners & success criteria):
- Create a per-request trace link prototype (owner: Riley Patel, due: 2026-08-05). Success: trace shows batching window, token count, model variant used; CS uses it in 3 triages without extra logs.
- Publish SDK tokenization reconciliation script as GH gist + run internal audit on 10 customers (owner: Maya Singh, due: 2026-08-02). Success: reduces billing confusion tickets by measurable delta.
- Add a new Console toggle for "Latency-first" preset (feature flag behind experiment) and roll out to 5 beta customers (owner: Product: Priya Das; Eng: Liam O'Connor). Success: beta customers see median latency improvement >=20% for interactive routes.

Engineering blockers (detailed):
- Missing per-route batching metric signal in tracing pipeline (JIRA-4982): currently we have only global batching stats and per-model throughput. Need to add route_id -> batching-window histograms exported to tracing. Blocker: minor schema change in trace collector + downstream indexing.
- Tokenization mismatch: SDK uses a vendored tokenizer with different special-case handling for function-calls. Blocker: need a canonical tokenization service or a shared utility lib across SDKs. Impact: affects billing and evaluation pipelines. Related to JIRA-5011.
- Private deploy sample templates scattered across PRs; no single curated repo with a smoke-test pipeline. Blocker: lack of a cross-team owner and acceptance checklists.

Open questions we asked customers (and partial answers):
- Q: Would customers trade a small increase in nominal cost for better tail-latency? A: Mixed. Enterprise teams (SLAs) yes; SMBs no unless optional toggle.
- Q: How important is per-request billing trace vs per-route aggregated cost? A: For billing disputes, per-request is required. For optimization, per-route is usually sufficient.

Suggested risk-aware rollout plan for "Latency-first" preset:
1) Feature-flagged in Console (internal use only).
2) Beta to 5 customers who opt-in and have SLO requirements.
3) Monitor unit economics (tokens/second) and error rates for 30d.
4) Graduated release with a rollback plan (auto-fallback to previous preset).

Notes from the working session (raw, unedited):
- Maya: "We keep seeing token count disputes where a customer enabled streaming and their month jumped 2x — we need easy repros."
- Liam: "Collector should append route metadata to traces, it's one line change but needs coordination with storage indexers."
- Priya: "Customers repeatedly ask for a private-deploy quickstart repo—this is WCAG for us right now."
- Riley: "If we ship a latency-first preset without a fallback the economics get weird. We need a dynamic fallback policy in parallel."

Next steps (who does what):
- Riley P.: prototype per-request trace link (due 2026-08-05).
- Maya S.: tokenization script + audit (due 2026-08-02).
- Priya D.: owner for Private quickstart repo; create project board and assign infra Eng (due 2026-08-09).
- Avery C.: compile sample customer support threads + add to Confluence page linked above (due 2026-07-30).

Appendix: snippets & sample support thread excerpts (anonymized)
- "We see a huge bill jump after turning on streaming; is Redwood double-counting tokens? Our SDK shows 1.2M tokens, billing shows 2.3M." — DocsAssist support thread.
- "When we scaled from 60->200 RPS our 99th jumped to 1.2s, many timeouts — attaching load harness results." — RetailBot incident notes.

Unresolved / backlog ideas (lower priority):
- Auto-profiled route-splits: analyze traffic patterns and recommend splitting interactive vs batch traffic automatically.
- Route-level cost SLOs (budget caps per day).
- SDK lint rule to warn if tokenization differs significantly from backend on sample inputs.

If you want, I can:
- convert this into a one-pager for Eng leadership with required engineering hours and a proposed roadmap (2–3 slides), or
- open the minimum viable JIRA tickets for the quick wins and link them here.

Raw meeting attendees: Avery Chen (note-taker), Riley Patel, Maya Singh, Priya Das, Liam O'Connor, Jordan Neves
